newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Feb industrial output up 7.9 pct-FIEL.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Feb industrial output up 7.9 pct-FIEL.

text.p: Argentina's industrial production in February was 7.9 percent above the same month last year, according to data released by the private consultancy FIEL Monday.
For the first two months of the year, industrial output was up 10.6 percent on the same period of 1996, FIEL said.
Compared with the vacation month of January, the seasonally adjusted figure shows no change in output, while the non-seasonally adjusted increase was 7.2 percent.
FIEL said that of the 19 sectors comprising the industrial output index, six grew more than average in the first two months and seven grew less than average.

The biggest growth was for the auto sector, up 67.3 percent, followed by petrochemicals, up 33.7 percent, cement, up 29.1 percent, tires, up 21.9 percent, agrochemicals, up 15.5 percent and processed petrol, which rose 13.4 percent.

Electric domestic appliances grew 9.2 percent, drinks 6.5 percent, mineral chemicals 6.0 percent, capital goods 5.4 percent, textile supplies 4.3 percent, non-electric domestic appliances 2.4 percent and pulp and paper 1.9 percent.

The six losers were aluminum, down 0.4 percent, cigarettes, down 0.8 percent, food, down 3.9 percent, plastic and rubber supplies, down 3.9 percent, iron and steel, which fell 6.4 percent, and tractors which dropped 7.7 percent.
